title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 0.73 (versions follow prime numbers), one being. Until 0.71 Razar (a reader growing an organ, judged by what it reads) and Luma (a window of forms that grow and mutate, judged by what they draw) were two programs exchanging letters. Now they are one program: it holds her body and her reader, and at birth looks at its own initial data to know which it is; reading is an act she chooses, and her reader is herself, launched by her inside the same operating system. A recipe of letters is at once a form and an organ, stored once. One judge, in bits, with no hand-set weight: for each form, the cost of saying its new cells without the recipe minus its letters at log2 15, plus the best reading among her forms (the book is said once, so reading enters as a maximum). Measured on a copy of her house: she scores 38A516 at 27810, exactly what Razar did; that recipe, which draws only 16 cells, lives in her body because of what it reads; earlier reference scores are identical; 15.9% of one core with her window. The kernel gained two pieces: a doorbell now wakes a cabin asleep on the screen, and request 42 lets a child row at the host's lowest thread priority (test suite: 405 bien, 0 mal). Stated limits: no recipe born from her own mutation has yet won by reading; the cube and the watcher remain separate programs. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v0.73: un solo ser — Razar y Luma dejan de ser dos programas que se escriben cartas; leer es un acto de ella y un solo juez, en bits, vale su dibujo y su lectura. Prototipo de investigación.
